Initially I was concerned that VOAT lacked the depth and breadth of articles I was accustomed to seeing. Rather than bitch about it, I decided to try to augment what was here.

My biases probably effect to some extent, but I am genuinely interested in hearing all perspectives -- especially those I disagree with.

For now, things seem pretty good, but that only applies so long as a community's size stays below a certain critical threshold of activity, downvoat restrictions or otherwise. The problem is, the most popular opinions will still float to the top, regardless of downvoating, and that will cause dissenting opinions to be stuck at the bottom of the post, where most people won't ever see them, let alone voat on them. Even then, dissenting opinions can gain more visibility by latching on to the top-most comments as replies, but again, if you get enough people responding to the top comments, the dissenting opinions will still get buried.

It's not so much the nature of the platform as the nature of the people who use it, though. Most people on Reddit use upvote/downvote as a like/dislike or agree/disagree. It may not be as bad here, but it's still probably an issue. If people instead voated primarily on the basis of whether something was interesting, well thought out, and adds to the overarching discussion in some fashion, then the problem would be mitigated considerably.

this request seems predicated on a notion that political discourse ought to be balanced in some natural, intrinsic way. if this were the case, democratic systems could never come to any meaningful widely agreed-upon resolutions. the goal, i think, should be to reach consensus; naturally this won't happen on all subjects, but when society reaches consensus about something (an example: child labor; compare public opinion now to 100 years ago) it is resolved and no longer a source of conflict.

good political discourse will naturally include conflict among competing ideas, but we shouldn't proactively avoid agreement; it's how progress is made.

This is how totalitarian regimes think. There is not a clear cut way to run an economy, no Boolean value that you may assign. Most things are spectrums, and as such, it is hard for there to be a "way forward". We have learnt this from world war one and two. Thinking otherwise is foolish. Discussion and debate is healthy.

i encourage you to participate in an organization that never agrees on any course of action but instead concentrates only on healthy discussion and debate. you could report back about all the great things you guys accomplish.

the contention that some level of consensus is necessary for progress does not logically imply boolean correctness necessarily. suppose there are five possible approaches to solving a problem and fall on a spectrum of efficiency (or utilitarianism, or whatever your preferred measure of 'good'). further suppose that some of them are tied for best, so that you are right in that respect. some - perhaps all - of them will be better options than just discussing the merits of each endlessly. that is what i said the first time.

Wanted to share this because it was recently used in one of the apps I develop for and proved quite useful in so many ways. I'll try to break it down for anyone who wants to use this simple technique. The goal here is to quickly export MySQL data into Google Docs where it can be edited as a .gsheet. This does not include any information about the importing process at of the moment.

  1. Setup Google Drive to sync to a folder running inside your web server. You can now change the default folder to any directory. See here
  2. Using a langauge like PHP I then exported the dynamic data from MYSQL to a .csv file (comma deliminated) and save that to a specified folder. I used .CSV format.
 // Get the content that is in the buffer and put it in your file // 
file_put_contents('folder/filename.csv', ob_get_contents());
  1. At this point a file is created in the "folder" directory and is synced to Google Drive. Then when I visited http://drive.google.com all my exported files were automatically synced.
  2. From here its all about throwing everything together like adding dynamic filenames (so files do NOT overwrite) and tweaking the csv format takes a little time but not much.

If anyone has any comments, or needs more info just let me know. I am happy to help! :)
